question_canonical: Describe your proposed approach to data conversion from legacy ERP systems into Oracle Cloud Fusion.
answer_text: iteria runs conversion as a controlled workstream with source profiling, mapping workshops, iterative mock loads, and reconciliation sign-off before cutover. We use Oracle Cloud tools plus proven conversion accelerators from prior public-sector Fusion deployments, with client SMEs validating financials, HCM, and payroll balances at each mock.

question_canonical: How will you support single sign-on and identity integration with the agency's identity provider?
answer_text: We configure Oracle Cloud Fusion Federation / SSO against the agency IdP (Azure AD, Okta, or SAML 2.0) using the agency's identity standards. Role provisioning follows least privilege and is tested with named personas before go-live.

question_canonical: Describe your project management methodology and governance structure for an Oracle Cloud ERP implementation.
answer_text: iteria uses a stage-gated delivery model with a named project manager, weekly steering, RAID log, and decision register. Scope, schedule, and risks are reviewed with the agency project sponsor; change control is written and approved before work shifts.

question_canonical: What is your approach to Chart of Accounts design and financials configuration in Oracle Cloud Fusion?
answer_text: We design the CoA to support statutory reporting, grants, and management reporting without over-segmenting. Workshops capture fund, department, project, and account structures; configuration is proven through conference room pilots and period-close rehearsals.

question_canonical: How do you handle payroll parallel testing and go-live readiness?
answer_text: Payroll readiness includes configuration validation, multiple parallel payroll cycles, tax and deduction reconciliations, and employee sample audits. Cutover proceeds only after the agency payroll lead signs the parallel results and exception plan.

question_canonical: Describe your training and knowledge-transfer approach for end users and system administrators.
answer_text: Training is role-based: process owners first, then end-user cohorts, with admin runbooks for support staff. We deliver workshops, recorded sessions, and job aids tied to the agency's configured processes rather than generic product demos.

question_canonical: How will you meet security, CJIS, SOC 2, or NIST control requirements applicable to this engagement?
answer_text: Oracle Cloud Fusion provides the baseline cloud controls; iteria maps agency control requirements to configuration, access design, and operational procedures. Evidence packs and control narratives are assembled with the agency CISO / compliance lead during design and before go-live.

question_canonical: What is included in post-go-live hypercare and ongoing support?
answer_text: Hypercare covers a defined window with on-site or remote support, severity-based response targets, and daily triage with the agency. After hypercare, support transitions to the agreed managed-services or warranty model with named contacts and escalation paths.

question_canonical: Describe your approach to Procure-to-Pay configuration including approvals and supplier onboarding.
answer_text: We configure requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, and payables to match the agency's approval policy and fund controls. Supplier onboarding, catalogs, and invoice matching rules are tested with real document samples before cutover.

question_canonical: How do you approach HCM core HR, position control, and benefits configuration?
answer_text: HCM design starts with the agency's position and job structures, then workflows for hire, transfer, and termination. Benefits and eligibility rules are configured with HR and validated through life-event scenarios before production load.

question_canonical: Can you support integrations with existing agency systems (timekeeping, tax, banking, GIS, etc.)?
answer_text: Yes. We inventory interfaces early, classify each as Oracle native, PaaS integration, or file-based, and document ownership, frequency, and error handling. Critical interfaces are built and tested in the CRP / SIT cycles before UAT.

question_canonical: Describe your testing strategy (unit, SIT, UAT, payroll parallel).
answer_text: Testing is planned by process, not by module alone. Unit and SIT prove configuration and integrations; UAT is agency-led with iteria facilitation; payroll and financials run dedicated parallels with reconciliation criteria agreed in writing.

question_canonical: What differentiates iteria from other Oracle Cloud implementation partners?
answer_text: iteria focuses on public-sector Fusion delivery with practitioners who have taken agencies live. We bring reusable conversion, testing, and cutover patterns from prior municipal and county work, and we write proposals and delivery plans in the agency's process language.

question_canonical: How do you manage organizational change management (OCM) during the ERP transformation?
answer_text: OCM runs alongside delivery: stakeholder map, change impacts by role, communications calendar, and super-user network. Adoption metrics and office hours continue through hypercare so issues surface early.

question_canonical: Describe your approach to reporting, OTBI, and analytics / OAC for public-sector clients.
answer_text: We prioritize the agency's statutory and management reports first, map them to Fusion subject areas or OAC, and retire shadow spreadsheets where Fusion can own the truth. Report owners validate samples before go-live.

question_canonical: How will budget control, encumbrances, and funds management be configured?
answer_text: Budget configuration follows the agency's fund accounting rules, including encumbrance points and override policy. We validate budget check behavior with real scenarios from finance before opening purchasing in production.

question_canonical: What is your approach to inventory, assets, or supply chain modules when in scope?
answer_text: Scope modules are configured against the agency's item masters, warehouses, and asset policies. We sequence master data, costing, and receiving processes so financials and inventory stay reconciled through cutover.

question_canonical: Provide an overview of your cutover and go-live checklist.
answer_text: Cutover is a timed runbook: final extracts, conversion load, reconciliation gates, security freeze windows, smoke tests, and go / no-go criteria owned by the agency sponsor. Rollback and interim operating procedures are documented before execution.

question_canonical: How do you handle public records, audit trails, and retention requirements?
answer_text: Fusion retains transactional history and audit attributes per Oracle Cloud capabilities; iteria aligns retention and export procedures with the agency records officer. Sensitive access is logged and reviewed with security.

question_canonical: Describe your staffing model, key personnel, and onshore / offshore mix.
answer_text: A named project manager and solution architect lead the engagement; functional leads cover FIN, HCM/Payroll, and technical tracks as scoped. Work that can be done remotely is coordinated to agency hours; critical workshops and cutover are staffed for live support.

question_canonical: How do you price change orders and out-of-scope requests?
answer_text: In-scope work follows the signed statement of work. Out-of-scope items are estimated, impact-assessed against schedule, and approved in writing before work begins. We do not silently absorb scope that threatens go-live quality.

question_canonical: Will you provide resumes and references for similar public-sector Oracle Cloud engagements?
answer_text: Yes. We provide key personnel resumes and client references from comparable Fusion implementations, subject to client permission. Reference conversations can be scheduled during evaluation.

question_canonical: Describe your disaster recovery and business continuity approach for the proposed solution.
answer_text: Oracle Cloud Fusion provides Oracle-managed DR capabilities for the SaaS service. iteria documents RPO/RTO expectations with the agency, validates admin recovery procedures, and includes continuity steps in the cutover and support runbooks.

question_canonical: How do you ensure accessibility (ADA / Section 508) for users of the system and training materials?
answer_text: Oracle Cloud Fusion targets Oracle's accessibility standards for the SaaS UI. Training materials and agency-facing artifacts we produce follow accessible document practices, and we coordinate with the agency ADA coordinator on any local requirements.
